transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, I made this appointment because I've been having these really strange experiences lately. I'm a teaching assistant, and... well, what scares me most right now is that when I walk across campus, it just feels like I’m watching everything through a pane of glass. 

It's hard to explain, but it's like I’m not fully in my own body, and the buildings and all the students around me just seem slightly unreal. It's really unsettling, and it's been bothering me enough that I felt like I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.

When you feel like you're watching everything through a pane of glass and things seem unreal, do you know that this is just how your mind is perceiving things, or do you believe that the world around you has actually become unreal?

No, I... I know it's just my mind. I don't actually believe the world has turned fake or anything like that. Logically, I know the campus is exactly the same as it always is, and the students are real. It's just that my perception is off, I guess. Knowing it's in my head doesn't really make the feeling go away, though.
When you experience these feelings of watching through glass and things seeming unreal, do you also notice your heart racing, difficulty breathing, or a sense of panic during these episodes?

No, not really. I don't feel panicked when it happens, and my heart doesn't race or anything like that. I breathe just fine. It's really just that weird, detached feeling, like I'm disconnected from everything around me, but physically I feel normal.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed changes in your mood, such as feeling persistently sad or down, or have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Well, I wouldn't say I feel persistently sad, like crying or anything. It's more that... I just can't seem to feel any good emotions right now. 

Like, the other day my husband cut some flowers from our garden and tried to make me tea. I knew it was a really kind thing for him to do, but... I just couldn’t feel the warmth or the pleasure I normally would from something like that. It was just this blank heaviness instead. So I guess I have lost interest, in a way, because I just can't seem to feel the joy in it anymore.
How long have you been experiencing this blank heaviness and inability to feel pleasure in things? Has it been going on for a few weeks, or longer?

No, it hasn't been a few weeks. It's been... well, exactly six days. It started right after the lighting rig collapsed during the showcase. Ever since that happened, I've just felt this way. So, yeah, just the last six days.

Since the lighting rig collapsed six days ago, have you been having unwanted memories or flashbacks of that event, or do you find yourself avoiding places or situations that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. The memories just... they kind of come out of nowhere. The sound of that rig coming down keeps barging into my head when I’m just sitting there grading, or even when I'm just making coffee. And when it happens, suddenly I can see the volunteer on the floor, and all the students pushing forward... it feels exactly like it’s happening right in front of me all over again.
When you think about going back to campus or to the theater where the lighting rig collapsed, do you find yourself actively avoiding those places, or do you try to go there despite the discomfort?

I definitely try to avoid it. I've actually been taking the long way around campus just so I don't have to walk past the atrium where it happened. And it's not just the place... if I'm talking to someone and they even mention the showcase, I just immediately change the subject. Or I'll just find an excuse to leave the room so I don't have to talk about it or think about it. I just can't deal with it right now.

Besides the feeling of watching through glass and things seeming unreal, have you noticed any other changes in how you perceive your own body or sense of self—like feeling disconnected from your arms or legs, or like you're observing yourself from outside your body?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Honestly, that's the part that scares me most. When I walk across campus, it really does feel like I’m watching everything through glass. It's just this strange sensation like... like I’m not fully in my own body. And everything around me—the buildings, the students walking by—they all just seem slightly unreal. So, yeah, I definitely feel that disconnect from myself.

When you're not thinking about the lighting rig collapse or the showcase, do you still experience that blank heaviness and inability to feel pleasure, or does it mainly happen when memories of the event come up?

It's pretty much there all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about the collapse. Like, just the other day, my husband cut some flowers from the garden and tried to make me tea. I knew it was a really kind thing for him to do, but... I just couldn’t feel the warmth or pleasure I normally would from something like that. I just felt that same blank heaviness. It's like I just can't feel the good things right now, no matter what is going on around me.
